questions.question_text_en: Why do we need to have established and fair procedures in the governance of society?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: To make people feel their freedom may be constrained.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To enhance the awareness of citizens regarding rule of law and its predictability.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: To help and comfort regional governments in their daily routines.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To deny the federal government manage its day-to-day activities.

explanation.solution_text_en: Fair and established procedures make public power predictable and subject to law. This supports rule of law because citizens and officials can know the rules in advance and expect them to be applied consistently.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Understanding Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: The absence of rule of law could cause
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the possible replacement of the state with individual cooperation's.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: make people believe to live even without the existence of the state.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: anarchy, crisis, dictatorship and could even leads to state collapse.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: no major problem in social life.

explanation.solution_text_en: Rule of law restrains arbitrary power and provides an orderly framework for resolving disputes. When it is absent, instability, arbitrary rule, serious conflict and even state breakdown can follow.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3: Democracy; Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: What roles do individuals and institutions have in combating corruption?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: When government believes that it is its exclusive domain to combat it.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: When the public assigns the task as purely a government engagement.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: When individuals demonstrate civility and institutions demonstrate transparency and accountability to combat it.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: When they act separately to check it.

explanation.solution_text_en: Current citizenship education treats integrity, civic responsibility, transparency and accountability as mutually reinforcing. Citizens should reject corrupt practices, while institutions should make decisions and public resources open to scrutiny.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1; Grade 10 - Unit 3

questions.question_text_en: How do we explain the equality and burdens that nations, nationalities and peoples have in Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The three groups are equal and their interaction generates mutual burdens they have to shoulder.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Equality and burdens of the three group is determined by the size of their population and territory.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Nationalities could be justified to think to have more rights than peoples.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Nations are more equal than others.

explanation.solution_text_en: The constitutional and multicultural approach rejects ranking peoples by population size or territory. Equal respect and shared responsibility are consistent with unity in diversity and peaceful coexistence.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6: Multiculturalism; National Unity through Diversity

questions.question_text_en: Public desire means the promotion of the interest of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: distinguished personalities.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the general public in a country.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: groups working against the society.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: people living control the power of government only.

explanation.solution_text_en: Public interest refers to the welfare or common good of the wider community, not the private advantage of selected officials, personalities or groups.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about duties and rights of citizens in a democracy?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: B is the closest/intended option, but its wording makes enjoyment of rights sound conditional on duties. The current curriculum treats rights and responsibilities as complementary, while fundamental rights remain inherent.  ESSLCE / EUEE Civics and Ethical Education | 2013 E.C. | Curriculum-Aligned Study Guide
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Protecting a country's border against external aggression belongs to citizens' rights.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Citizens enjoy their rights to the maximum only when they accomplish their duties.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Citizens are entitled to their rights without any consideration of obligations.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Constitutional obligations and constitutional rights are mutually exclusive.

explanation.solution_text_en: The intended idea is that democratic citizenship combines rights with responsibilities. However, current human-rights teaching also stresses that fundamental human rights are inherent and inalienable; they are not rewards that a person earns only after performing duties.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; FDRE Constitution, Arts. 10-13

questions.question_text_en: Mohammed always thinks twice before making a decision or an action once. This characteristic shows his dedication to rely on
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: an unnecessarily fast decision-making method

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a risk-free decision making

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a slow decision-making procedure

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a reasonable decision making

explanation.solution_text_en: Thinking before acting, considering alternatives and weighing likely consequences are characteristics of rational decision-making rather than simply making a slow or supposedly risk-free choice.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: In order to undertake scientific research, accumulate knowledge and make good policies, we need to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: use an artificially created data

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: do a verified data analysis

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: arbitrarily analyze data

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: copy it from other places

explanation.solution_text_en: Sound research and public policy require information that is checked, analyzed and interpreted systematically. Fabricated or arbitrary data cannot provide a reliable basis for knowledge or decisions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: One of the best and appropriate ways of developing a reading habit is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: always reading non fictional books

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: always reading fictional books

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: start with simple reading materials and making a progress

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: giving more time to audio-books

explanation.solution_text_en: A practical way to build a reading habit is to begin with manageable material, read consistently and gradually increase difficulty and range. Restricting oneself permanently to only fiction or only non-fiction is unnecessary.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills / learning skills

questions.question_text_en: To be accepted as a responsible member of a society and enjoy a successful social life, one has to be
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: an honest person

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a politician in the African context

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a broker only maximizing his/her gain

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a businessman only seeking profit

explanation.solution_text_en: Honesty is a core ethical value that builds trust and supports responsible social life. The other choices define people mainly by occupation or private gain rather than by ethical conduct.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: When citizens are disengaged from their political, economic and social activities, they are exhibiting characteristics of being
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: active

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: impartial

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: passive

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: legal

explanation.solution_text_en: Citizens who withdraw from political, economic and social participation display passive citizenship. Active citizenship requires informed and constructive participation in community and public affairs.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: When an individual frees himself/herself from being dominated by others, this helps to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: develop an aggressive character.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: let others decide on his/her behalf.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: save money, be self-reliant and plan the future

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: develop a quite character and a passive life.

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-reliance involves reducing avoidable dependence on others, planning for the future, managing resources responsibly and making one's own informed decisions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 4: Consumption, Saving and Investment; Grade 9 Citizenship - Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: When countries receive financial aid from other countries, they are expected to give away a portion of their sovereignty. This is a typical problem caused by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: independence

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: normal and healthy politics

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: dependency

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Colonialism

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency describes a relationship in which weaker economies may become strongly reliant on external resources and influence. Such reliance can reduce policy autonomy and bargaining power.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 5 & 6: Trade and Finance; Economic Development

questions.question_text_en: Dawit always weighs among choices available with a sober mind for the best outcome. This shows Dawit is a
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: rational and an informed person

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: self-centered person

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: self-sacrificing person

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: time-wasting person

explanation.solution_text_en: A person who compares available alternatives calmly and selects the option with the best expected outcome is acting rationally and on the basis of information.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: In order to avail capital for investment, get an interest and place money in a safe environment, people must deposit their money in
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Banks

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Their own houses

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Equb stores

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Iddir centers

explanation.solution_text_en: Banks mobilize deposits, keep funds in a regulated financial system and channel savings toward lending and investment. Depending on the account, depositors may also receive interest.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 4 & 5: Saving; Trade and Finance

questions.question_text_en: One of the following is a means of reversing dependency.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Conducting a socialist revolution

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Increasing imports from developed countries

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Eradicating poverty

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Negotiating with developed countries to end unequal relationship

explanation.solution_text_en: Reducing poverty strengthens domestic productive capacity, human development and economic independence. In current development teaching, sustained poverty reduction is therefore a central route away from harmful dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 6: Economic Development; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 6: Poverty and Inequality

secondary_curriculum_links: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 6: Poverty and Inequality

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is among the strategies to develop self-confidence?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Know your strengths and weaknesses

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Become more arrogant

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Underestimate others

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Don't accept your mistakes

explanation.solution_text_en: Realistic self-confidence begins with self-knowledge. Recognizing strengths and weaknesses makes it possible to improve, seek help when needed and set achievable goals without becoming arrogant.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a personal quality of a self-reliant person?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Lacking integrity

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Extravagant

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Making good decisions

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Pessimistic about prospects

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-reliance requires the ability to assess a situation and make responsible decisions. Lack of integrity, wastefulness and pessimism undermine rather than strengthen self-reliance.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Good decision making requires
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: doing the right thing without bothering about the moral nature of the situation.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: sensitivity to moral issues.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: giving priority to economic benefits without considering moral components.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: an immediate action without examining the pros and cons of the decision.

explanation.solution_text_en: Good decisions are not only efficient; they also consider whether an action is right, fair and respectful of others. Sensitivity to the moral dimension of a problem is therefore essential.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7: Ethical Values; Problem Solving

questions.question_text_en: Abebe is not an extravagant person because he
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: buys things though he does not need them.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: buys things without planning.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: spends his money wisely.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: spends more money than he can afford.

explanation.solution_text_en: Avoiding extravagance means planning expenditure and using money according to needs and priorities. Spending wisely is the only option that reflects responsible consumption.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 4: Consumption, Saving and Investment

questions.question_text_en: According to the FDRE Constitution, sovereignty resides in the
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: communities.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: nations, nationalities and peoples.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: professional associations.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: religious groups.

explanation.solution_text_en: Article 8 of the FDRE Constitution states that sovereign power resides in the Nations, Nationalities and Peoples of Ethiopia and is expressed through representatives and direct democratic participation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; Grade 10 - Unit 5; FDRE Constitution Art. 8

questions.question_text_en: The separation of power is expressed through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the workings of the organs of government based on checks and balances.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the exercise of professionalism among journalists.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the willingness of ministers to do what is right and proper.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the commitment leaders show for the principles of democracy.

explanation.solution_text_en: Separation of powers assigns different public functions to different organs and is reinforced by checks and balances. Its purpose is to limit concentration and abuse of governmental power.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following rights differs with regard to the domain of human rights?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The right to privacy.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The right to property.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The right to liberty.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The right to life.

explanation.solution_text_en: Life, liberty and privacy are commonly grouped as civil or personal rights, while property has a strong economic dimension. That makes property the different item in this set.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: What are the ways for people to participate in the decision-making process at the level of kebeles?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Thinking for personal gains than what advances the interest of community.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Actively participating in matters that affect members of kebele.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Regularly attending meetings when officials of kebeles ask for.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Showing respect to those working there.

explanation.solution_text_en: Local democratic participation is meaningful when residents take part in issues and decisions that affect their kebele and community, rather than attending only when summoned or focusing on private gain.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: The exclusive power that the federal government holds manifests through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: educational and health under takings.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the rights that it shares with regional states

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: foreign policies, defense and finance.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the collection of taxes.

explanation.solution_text_en: The federal level is responsible for core national functions such as foreign affairs, national defense and major monetary/financial matters. Education, health and taxation include significant state or shared responsibilities.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: When an organization is founded and operated by individuals that dispense their knowledge, time and energy free of charge, then the organization can be considered as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a share company.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a voluntary organization.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a multi-national corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a religious organization.

explanation.solution_text_en: An organization based on people freely contributing time, knowledge or labor without being compelled or paid as owners is characteristically a voluntary organization.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Civic participation and social organizations

questions.question_text_en: Members of a state who fulfill their respective duties effectively are best described as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: political leaders

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: religious leaders

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: senior citizens

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: responsible citizens

explanation.solution_text_en: Citizens who perform their lawful and civic duties responsibly are best described as responsible citizens, regardless of age, occupation or leadership position.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Fulfilling one's responsibility legally and politically results in
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a Parochial political culture

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: rewarding consequences

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: punishing consequences

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a one side political culture

explanation.solution_text_en: Responsible fulfillment of lawful and political duties supports trust, social order and participation, producing constructive rather than punitive consequences for civic life.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Paying fair tax, respecting the laws of the land and respecting the rights of others is considered as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: social obligations.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: commercial obligations.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: legal obligations.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: moral obligations.

explanation.solution_text_en: Paying taxes and obeying law are explicit legal duties; respecting the legally protected rights of others is also part of lawful civic conduct. The set is therefore best classified as legal obligations.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice; Grade 10 Citizenship - Unit 6

questions.question_text_en: When people learn to protect natural vegetation and engage in re-afforestation, this shows an awareness of people with their
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: environment.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: economic benefits.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: political interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: social independence.

explanation.solution_text_en: Protecting vegetation and reforestation show environmental awareness because these actions conserve ecosystems, soils and other natural resources.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 8: Economy, Environment and Climate Change

questions.question_text_en: Which one is a cardinal element of due process of law?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Right to look for a political alternative.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Right to assembly

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Right to demonstration

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Right to counsel

explanation.solution_text_en: Due process requires a fair legal procedure for a person accused or affected by state action. Access to legal counsel is a core safeguard because it helps a person understand and defend his or her rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights / rule of law

questions.question_text_en: Apart from rules, laws are enacted by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: associations

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Parliament

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the Council of Ministers

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: individuals

explanation.solution_text_en: In a constitutional system, primary legislation is enacted by the legislature or parliament. Executive bodies may issue regulations within authority granted by law, but they do not replace parliament as the law-making body.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is different in relation to corruption?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The primary instrument to control corruption is indeed the rule of law but religious institutions and others do have roles to play on the moral side of social life.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Persons with authority cannot comply with the rule of law to put corruption under control.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Schools in general and higher institutions of learning in particular should work to raise social awareness to succeed with the campaign against corruption.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Corrupt persons and office holders should face legal retributions for their wrong doings.

explanation.solution_text_en: Option B contradicts anti-corruption principles: persons exercising public authority are required to comply with the law. Rule of law, education, ethical standards and legal accountability can all contribute to controlling corruption.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Understanding Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: The peasant rebellion which broke out in Gojjam in 1968 against the central authority was mainly caused by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: external intervention

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the request for democratic elections

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the demand for autonomy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the burden of taxation

explanation.solution_text_en: The current Grade 12 History textbook explains that the 1968 Gojjam rebellion was provoked in large part by a new agricultural income tax law and changes in land measurement. Tax burden is therefore the best answer.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6: Ethiopia, 1941-1991

questions.question_text_en: ln 1991, Derg was over thrown due to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: mediation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: diplomatic effort

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: an armed struggle

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a peaceful transition of power

explanation.solution_text_en: The Derg regime collapsed in 1991 after prolonged armed conflicts and major military defeats; the transition was not primarily the result of mediation or a negotiated peaceful transfer.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6: Ethiopia, 1941-1991

questions.question_text_en: Transparency is all about
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: to be responsible for consequences of the work done.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: allowing others to inspect what an office bearer are doing.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: to be efficient at work as office holder.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: keeping what officials are doing as secret.

explanation.solution_text_en: Transparency means openness: public institutions make relevant processes, decisions and information accessible so that citizens and oversight bodies can inspect and understand what office holders are doing.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Understanding Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: The importance of political tolerance in Ethiopia could be expressed through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: becoming arrogant to force others to accept the official's position,

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: disrespect to the concerns that others are displaying.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: showing civility and respect for the viewpoints of others.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: advancing one's own view points as the best.

explanation.solution_text_en: Political tolerance means accepting that other citizens may hold different views and treating them with civility and respect. It is the opposite of forcing, insulting or dismissing others.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: What advantages federalism has to offer for Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Making groups take turn to rule over others.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To allow nations, nationalities and peoples to think of separation from Ethiopia.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Making nations, nationalities and peoples believe that their differences are more important than what unite them.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Advances development through genuine self-rule and shared rule.

explanation.solution_text_en: Federalism combines self-rule in constituent units with shared rule at the federal level. In a diverse society, this arrangement can support participation, accommodation of diversity and development while preserving common institutions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is different regarding federal and regional state constitutions?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: The stem says "different" but the choices read more like a request for the correct statement. A is the closest answer; the item is poorly worded.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The goal of the federal and regional constitutions is to promote ethnic groups to exercise self-administration

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The constitutions of FDRE has not brought an end to the unitary form of government,

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Both the federal and regional constitutions have no clear boundary in their exercise of power.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The regional states constitutions are in parity with the federal one.

explanation.solution_text_en: A is the only option broadly consistent with the constitutional purpose of enabling self-government within a federal order. The other choices conflict with current teaching: the FDRE is federal rather than unitary, powers are constitutionally allocated, and regional constitutions operate within the federal constitutional framework.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5; Grade 12 History - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: What role the rule of law has in the democratization of society?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Rule of law gives the governed unlimited right to question officials.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Good hearted officials always do the right thing even in the absence of rule of law.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Rule of law suppresses the governed than the governing.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Rule of law is instrumental to create limited government and help enhance democracy.

explanation.solution_text_en: Rule of law makes government legally limited and accountable instead of unlimited or personal. This is one of the institutional conditions that supports democracy and protects citizens.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3

questions.question_text_en: Justice in the areas of social services should focus on and support for
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: sympathy for wealthy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: gender bias

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Segregation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: fairness in distribution

explanation.solution_text_en: Justice in social services requires fair and equitable access and distribution, especially where needs differ. Sympathy for wealth, segregation and gender bias contradict fairness.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights / equality and non-discrimination

questions.question_text_en: The duties attached to courts may NOT include one of the following
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: interpreting law.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: protection of' human rights.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: pursuing criminals to bring to justice.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: performing duties independently.

explanation.solution_text_en: Courts interpret and apply law, protect rights through adjudication and should act independently. Investigation and pursuit of suspected criminals are primarily functions of police and prosecution, not the court itself.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance / justice institutions

questions.question_text_en: The rights of tax payers have include
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: running business based on established legal systems.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: evading taxes.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: bribing tax collection officers.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: engaging in illicit trade.

explanation.solution_text_en: Among the choices, operating a lawful business is the only legitimate taxpayer-related activity. Tax evasion, bribery and illicit trade violate law and cannot be treated as taxpayer rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Patriotic citizen means
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: not to be concerned with the democratization of society

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: to be willing to provide the public what is necessary in times of crisis.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: to be less concerned to keep ethical values of society.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: to promote private interests over the public ones.

explanation.solution_text_en: Patriotism includes willingness to serve the common good and assist the public in times of need or crisis. It is not the rejection of democracy, ethics or the public interest.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following could be a reflection of patriotism?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: To promote private interest over that of the public.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To promote personal interests at the expense of the public.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Upholding the Constitution and respect to other laws of the country.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Participation in the affairs that are strictly private.

explanation.solution_text_en: Respecting the Constitution and other laws is a concrete civic expression of patriotism because it supports the constitutional order and the rights of fellow citizens.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Which one is a proper way of fighting against the pandemic of COVID-19 at a global level?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Continuing under state of emergency ends until the pandemic ends

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Taking homemade remedies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Quarantining COVID-19 patients

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Applying preventive measures effectively

explanation.solution_text_en: For a communicable disease such as COVID-19, effective preventive measures - including evidence-based public-health precautions - are broader and more appropriate than relying on unverified remedies or indefinite emergency rule.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: When you are responsible for your actions, you will
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: disrespect the norms and values of the society

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: be able to develop a sense of reliance

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: be able to utilize your own fundamental rights

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: sacrifice your fundamental rights

explanation.solution_text_en: Accepting responsibility for one's choices strengthens self-reliance because a person learns to own consequences, correct mistakes and make better future decisions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: How is work believed to be an instrument for development?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The difference between the poor and rich countries cannot be attributed to work.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: In some cases, development may be achieved when you don't have to work.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The development we see around is due to the human capacity to change himself and his surroundings.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The human capacity to work has created all our problems.

explanation.solution_text_en: Work contributes to development because human effort, skills and innovation transform resources and surroundings into goods, services and improved living conditions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 6 & 7: Economic Development; Sectors and Strategies

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is correct about work ethics?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Establishing a 'smoking' zone with in the work place is an essential part of labor discipline in work ethics.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Doing things isolated from the other members of the work force maximizes efficiency.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Entertaining with co-workers during working hours creates a harmony which in turn increases productivity.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A proper utilization of equipment and utilities is an essential element of work ethics.

explanation.solution_text_en: Work ethics include care for organizational resources, discipline, responsibility and efficient use of equipment and utilities. Wasting work time or isolating oneself is not a general principle of good work conduct.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Applied Ethics

questions.question_text_en: What is the negative effect of dependency of developing countries on the developed countries?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Enables developed countries to exercise significant control on the economic development.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Enables developing countries to sell manufactured goods to developed countries through free market policy principle.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Creates permanent growth that promotes sustainable development and economic independence of developing countries.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Inhibits the domestic and self-sustained growth of developed countries in favor of developing countries.

explanation.solution_text_en: A harmful form of dependency can give more powerful external actors substantial influence over the development choices of weaker economies. Sustainable development instead seeks stronger domestic capacity and resilience.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 5 & 6

questions.question_text_en: Which one is a characteristic feature of devolution of power?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A power share mechanism among politically independent sovereign countries

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Distribution of power from the center to regional government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Monopoly of power by the central government

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Concentration of power in the center

explanation.solution_text_en: Devolution transfers meaningful authority from a central government to regional or local governments. It is a form of decentralization, not a concentration or monopoly of power at the center.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia's foreign policy is based on all of the following principles except
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Confrontation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Co-existence

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: People to people diplomacy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Cooperation

explanation.solution_text_en: Current citizenship material presents foreign relations in terms of peaceful coexistence, cooperation, diplomacy and national interest. Confrontation is therefore the exception among the listed principles.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa

questions.question_text_en: Recently, Ethiopian and South Sudanese elders exchanged visits along the border between the two countries in order to take their overall relation to a higher level. Type of diplomacy is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Elite diplomacy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Shuttle diplomacy

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Gun-boat diplomacy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Public diplomacy

explanation.solution_text_en: Visits and relationship-building by elders and communities are examples of people-to-people or public diplomacy, because non-state members of the public contribute to relations across borders.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Foreign Relations

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about the amendment procedure of FDRE constitution?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: No option is fully correct. A is the closest because the House of Peoples' Representatives participates in amendment, but the Constitution establishes a shared, multi-institutional procedure.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Power of amendment of the constitution belongs to the House of People Representatives.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The power to amend the constitution lays in the hands of the council of ministers.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The first amendment to the FDRE constitution was made by the Transitional Government.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The mandate to amend the constitution belongs to the constituent assembly.

explanation.solution_text_en: The House of Peoples' Representatives has an important role in initiating and approving constitutional amendments, but it does not hold the amendment power alone. Articles 104-105 also require roles for the House of the Federation and State Councils, with thresholds depending on the provision being amended.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; FDRE Constitution Arts. 104-105

questions.question_text_en: Among the different ways of conflict management, one proceeds with a direct discussion among disputants and, thus, avoids an outside party. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Mediation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Negotiation

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Litigation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Arbitration

explanation.solution_text_en: Negotiation is direct discussion between the parties to a dispute in an effort to reach agreement. Mediation and arbitration involve a third party, while litigation uses a court.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution Mechanisms

questions.question_text_en: Identify the correct statement about political parties versus pressure groups.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The former is an association of advocacy groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The latter officially compete in the country's elections for political power.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The former reflects always the views of marginalized groups.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The latter try to influence government to be more responsive to the wishes of the people.

explanation.solution_text_en: Pressure or interest groups generally seek to influence public policy without themselves competing to form a government. Political parties, by contrast, normally organize to contest elections and exercise political power.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is NOT part of the major sources of knowledge?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: heredity

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: understanding nature

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: experimentation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: information

explanation.solution_text_en: Heredity can affect biological traits but it is not normally classified as a source from which a person obtains knowledge. Observation of nature, experimentation and information can all contribute to knowledge.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Identify the correct statement about information, knowledge and wisdom.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Knowledge is the ability to use wisdom.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Wisdom always contradicts with social values.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Knowledge is the ability to use information.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Knowledge helps us to develop information.

explanation.solution_text_en: Information consists of organized facts or messages; knowledge develops when information is understood and can be applied. Wisdom goes further by using knowledge with sound judgment.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: The information that is collected and analyzed for a specific purpose will help to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: formulate a hypothesis.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: make knowledge-based decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: avoid judgment.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: avoid generalization.

explanation.solution_text_en: Information gathered and analyzed for a defined purpose helps people make evidence-based or knowledge-based decisions. It does not require them to avoid judgment or generalization altogether.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which method explains the skill of using information properly?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Reproducing new information using unscientific methods.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Using observation as an ultimate source of information.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Making a quick decision based on first-hand information.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Identifying, evaluating and managing information.

explanation.solution_text_en: Information literacy involves identifying what information is needed, evaluating its quality and relevance, organizing it and using it responsibly. That is more complete than relying on a single observation or quick decision.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7; Unit 2: Digital Technology

questions.question_text_en: Why do we need the separation of state and religion in Ethiopia? Because
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: None of the options states Article 11 accurately. The precise rule is separation of state and religion, no state religion, and no interference of one in the affairs of the other.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: they are always at war.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the former is for worldly governance and the later for heavenly reward.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the state is more important than what religion stands for.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the two are the same and different at the same time.

explanation.solution_text_en: The constitutional principle is that state and religion are institutionally separate and neither should dominate the other. B is the closest option because it distinguishes their spheres, although its phrase about "heavenly reward" is not the constitutional definition.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; FDRE Constitution Art. 11

questions.question_text_en: The concept of professionalism holds that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: professions shall be based on scientific principles to help one self and community.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: professions of all types offers equal payment.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: all professions are not manual.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: all professions produce similar pleasure for everyone.

explanation.solution_text_en: Professionalism requires competence, knowledge and ethical use of specialized skills in ways that serve both the practitioner and society. Equal pay or identical satisfaction across all professions is not part of its definition.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Applied Ethics

questions.question_text_en: Respecting labour discipline, punctuality and team work are attributes of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a good ethical work conduct

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the white human race

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: an in secured person

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the top management

explanation.solution_text_en: Punctuality, labor discipline, teamwork and responsible conduct are classic elements of ethical work behavior. They support reliability, cooperation and productivity.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Applied Ethics

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia's huge potential in agricultural and its industrial can be translated into action by increasing productivity and efficiency with the help of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the good will of donor-states

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: technological development

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: loan

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: NGO's

explanation.solution_text_en: Technology can raise productivity by improving methods, equipment, information and efficiency in agriculture and industry. Aid, loans and NGOs may play roles, but they are not substitutes for productivity-enhancing technological development.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 7: Main Sectors and Sectoral Policies of Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: The concept of the supremacy of the constitution refers to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the law of the land that is supreme, over all other laws.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the constitution is a set of laws that is derived from all other laws that a country has.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: other laws with different competence will not have to comply with the law of the land.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the absence of hierarchy of laws and the society.

explanation.solution_text_en: Constitutional supremacy means that the constitution is the highest law and inconsistent laws or state decisions have no legal effect. Article 9 of the FDRE Constitution expresses this principle.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3; FDRE Constitution Art. 9

questions.question_text_en: Genocide is labelled the worst crime against humanity because it
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: D is incomplete. The defining element is specific intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a protected group; merely committing an offense against a group is not by itself genocide.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: is confiscation of property

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: involves enslavement of people

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: is mass imprisonment of victims rather than killing

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: is committed against religious community or a group of people

explanation.solution_text_en: Genocide is exceptionally grave because it involves specified acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a protected national, ethnical, racial or religious group. D is the closest option because it points to group-targeted destruction, though it does not state the full legal definition.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: In Ethiopia, tax appropriately mainly because tax payment is to comply with tax laws and pay tax appropriately mainly because tax payment is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: chiefly used for charitable activities

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: used to purchase luxury items from abroad

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: mainly a moral obligation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a major source of revenue for government.

explanation.solution_text_en: Taxes are a major source of government revenue used to finance public services and public functions. The current Grade 12 Economics curriculum treats taxation as a key fiscal institution, not mainly as charity or luxury spending.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following achievements was a major accomplishment of the civil rights movement in the USA in 1950s?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Racism was over

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Slavery was abolished

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Segregation laws were dropped

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Women were given the right to vote

explanation.solution_text_en: A central achievement of the U.S. civil-rights movement was the dismantling of legally enforced racial segregation through court decisions and civil-rights legislation. Slavery had been abolished much earlier and women had gained federal voting rights before the 1950s.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 5: Global and Regional Developments Since 1945

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following ethical behaviors is associated with showing respect to people?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Civility

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Fairness

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Truthfulness

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Courage

explanation.solution_text_en: Civility means treating others politely and respectfully even when there is disagreement. It is therefore the ethical behavior most directly associated with showing respect to people.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia's leading role to the cause of Africa is symbolized her of the League
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's being the only African country as a member of the League of Nations.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ethiopia's transformation as the largest economy in the continent.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the opening of legations in Addis Ababa since 1896.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the establishment of the OAU/AU in Addis Ababa.

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethiopia's role in Pan-African cooperation is strongly symbolized by Addis Ababa hosting the founding of the Organization of African Unity in 1963 and continuing to host the African Union headquarters.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 7: Africa since the 1960s; Grade 9 Citizenship - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: Why is saving important for you? It
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: helps you to avoid a necessary spending.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: enables you to avoid all kinds of risks in life

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: enables you to deposit all of your income

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: helps you in the event of a financial emergency.

explanation.solution_text_en: Saving provides a financial buffer for emergencies and future needs. It does not mean avoiding all necessary spending or saving every unit of income.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 4: Consumption, Saving and Investment

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is correct about traditional saving institutions of Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The structures of Iquib and Idir are the same throughout the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Both Iquib and Idir are established by the mutual agreement of the community

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: ldir is a temporary saving association

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: lquib is always a long-term saving association

explanation.solution_text_en: Iqub and Idir are community-based institutions formed through voluntary mutual agreement, although their purposes and arrangements differ. Iqub is mainly rotating saving/credit, while Idir commonly provides mutual support in times of loss or emergency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 11 Economics - Saving

questions.question_text_en: Which one of following is NOT the reward of a sound economic system?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Skyrocketing prices

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Overall economic development

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Healthy market conditions

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: reduction of debt burden

explanation.solution_text_en: A sound economic system aims for stability, productive growth and manageable debt. Rapidly rising prices reduce purchasing power and are a macroeconomic problem rather than a reward.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Units 1 & 4: Macroeconomics; Policy Instruments

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following factors negatively affects community participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The existence of different outlooks within the community

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Willingness of members of the community to participate

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lack of awareness about the benefits of community participation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The existence of many effective good leaders

explanation.solution_text_en: People are less likely to participate when they do not understand the purpose or benefits of participation. Different viewpoints can be normal in a democratic community and do not by themselves prevent participation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a way of manifesting political participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Circulating fake news through the social media

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Campaigning for or against candidates during election

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Burning public institutions

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Disturbing democratic elections

explanation.solution_text_en: Campaigning peacefully for or against candidates is a lawful form of political participation. Spreading false information, damaging public institutions or disrupting elections undermines democratic participation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: When should we have to give rational criticism on government policies and strategies? When
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: policies are not keeping with the national interests.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: policies do not consider our own personal interests.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: strategies aim at benefiting the great majority of citizens.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: strategies are appropriate to solve socio-economic problems of the nation.

explanation.solution_text_en: Rational criticism should focus on the public interest and evidence. Policies that conflict with legitimate national interests are a proper subject of criticism; disagreement based only on private benefit is not a sufficient civic standard.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Ethiopia contributed to global peace and stability by
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: training and supporting some armed groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: intervening in the internal affairs of politically instable neighboring countries.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: allowing its soldiers to be employed as mercenaries.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: sending peace-keeping forces.

explanation.solution_text_en: Participation in international peacekeeping is a recognized way a country can support collective peace and security. Mercenary activity, armed-group support or improper intervention would not serve that purpose.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Foreign Relations; Grade 12 History - Unit 8

questions.question_text_en: What is meant by shouldering responsibility?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Fulfilling the duties expected from us

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Enjoying and exercising individual rights

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Be hard working to achieve personal goals

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Living for the enjoyment of others only

explanation.solution_text_en: Shouldering responsibility means accepting and carrying out duties for which one is accountable. Exercising rights is important, but it is not the definition of fulfilling responsibility.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: One of the following statements explains the duty of a good citizen.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Running for political positions

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Paying taxes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Joining in a professional organization

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Freedom of speech

explanation.solution_text_en: Paying legally required taxes is a civic duty. Freedom of speech is a right, while holding office or joining an organization are choices rather than universal duties.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice; Grade 10 Citizenship - Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: To carry out your responsibilities, you should
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: sacrifice some of your private interests

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: compromise the rights of others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: avoid your social life

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: liberate yourself from the domination of a community spirit

explanation.solution_text_en: Public responsibility can require reasonable sacrifice of some private convenience or interest for lawful common purposes. It never justifies violating the rights of others.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1; Grade 10 Citizenship - Unit 7

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following reasons justifies affirmative action for women?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Discrimination

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Non-discrimination

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Assimilation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Reverse discrimination

explanation.solution_text_en: Affirmative action is used to address the effects of historical or structural discrimination and unequal opportunity. In that sense, discrimination is the condition that provides the justification for corrective measures.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about the FDRE Constitution in terms or Nations, Nationalities and Peoples? The Constitution
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: D is the closest answer, but the Constitution protects both individual and collective rights. The wording "provides priority" is too broad.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: addresses the issue of nationalities by opting for a unitary state structure.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: places Nations, Nationalities and peoples under a single culture.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: has no provision for the right to secession.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: provides priority for group rights.

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE Constitution expressly recognizes collective rights of Nations, Nationalities and Peoples alongside individual human and democratic rights. D is the closest option, but "priority" should not be read as meaning group rights automatically override all individual rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6; FDRE Constitution

questions.question_text_en: The belief that one's culture is superior to others is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: multilateralism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: multiculturalism

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: pluralism

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: ethnocentrism

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethnocentrism is the belief or tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture and to regard one's own as superior. Multiculturalism and pluralism instead recognize diversity.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Multiculturalism in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: The concept of domestication involves
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: incorporating international treaties in to local laws of the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: using constitutional and ordinary laws mutually

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: replacing local laws with international laws

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: merging state and federal laws

explanation.solution_text_en: Domestication means giving an international treaty effect within a country's domestic legal order through the procedures required by that legal system. It does not simply replace all local law.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; constitutional law

questions.question_text_en: In a democratic system, the judiciary
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: D is the best general-democracy answer. Ethiopia's constitutional system gives final constitutional interpretation to the House of the Federation rather than ordinary courts.  ESSLCE / EUEE Civics and Ethical Education | 2013 E.C. | Curriculum-Aligned Study Guide
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: formulates the foreign policy of the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: is handled by prime minster

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: has seats in parliament

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: safeguards the constitution

explanation.solution_text_en: An independent judiciary safeguards legality and rights by applying the constitution and laws in cases before it. In Ethiopia specifically, however, final constitutional interpretation is assigned to the House of the Federation, so D should be understood in the general rule-of-law sense.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance / rule of law

questions.question_text_en: Truth is essential for social interaction for all of the following reasons except one. Which one?
questions.review_note: Item-quality note: Option B is grammatically damaged in the supplied exam text, so C is selected as the clearest answer from the preserved choices.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Using the instrument of knowledge for of interaction.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A mechanism of interaction based on proof myth.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Creating an interaction on the basis of myth.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Using scientific methods to realize a sound interaction.

explanation.solution_text_en: Truth-based social interaction relies on evidence, reliable knowledge and honest communication. Creating interaction on the basis of myth rather than evidence is therefore the clearest exception.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 7

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a major feature of rule of law?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Rule of man

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Constitutionalism

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Totalitarian rule

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Rule of divine

explanation.solution_text_en: Constitutionalism means government is limited and organized by constitutional rules rather than the personal will of rulers. It is therefore a major feature of rule of law.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism

questions.question_text_en: A type of democracy which is practiced through a referendum democracy is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: revolutionary democracy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: representative democracy

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: indirect democracy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: direct democracy

explanation.solution_text_en: A referendum lets citizens vote directly on a public question, so it is a form of direct democracy. Representative or indirect democracy operates mainly through elected representatives.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Authority differs from power in that, authority
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: is always illegitimate

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: is moral power

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: forces others to do what the power holder wants to do

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: is legal power

explanation.solution_text_en: Authority is power regarded as legitimate and exercised according to recognized legal or institutional rules. Mere power can exist without legitimacy or lawful authorization.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is correct about human and democratic rights?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Rights and obligations of citizens are outlined only in international declaration of human rights.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Citizens' rights and duties are not kept interdependently in democratic system.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Human and democratic rights are ensured by democratic governments

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: There is no correlation between constitutionalism on one hand and rights on the other.

explanation.solution_text_en: Democratic constitutional governments have a duty to respect, protect and help realize human and democratic rights. Rights are not created only by international declarations, and constitutionalism is closely connected to their protection.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: As it was seen from the economic history of developed countries, investment capital could be acquired through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: ignoring the agricultural sector and promoting the service sector.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: enduring in to an irresponsible level of debt.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: entering hard, getting money and saving.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: privatizing strategic national assets.

explanation.solution_text_en: Investment capital can be built through productive work, income generation and saving. Savings help finance investment directly or through financial institutions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 4: Consumption, Saving and Investment

questions.question_text_en: The most important international institutions in facilitating the global economy and finance are
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: IMF and World Bank.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: World Trade Organization.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: African Development Bank.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Chinese Exim bank

explanation.solution_text_en: The IMF and World Bank are major international financial institutions concerned with monetary cooperation, balance-of-payments support, development finance and related economic policy. The WTO is primarily a trade institution.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Unit 5: Trade and Finance

questions.question_text_en: An individual must carefully select his/her means of income in order to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: accumulate private property internationally.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: save more money at the time of divorce.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: hide his/her real income to escape taxation.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: live a legal, long lasting and happy life.

explanation.solution_text_en: Choosing a lawful and sustainable means of earning income supports long-term wellbeing and responsible citizenship. Hiding income to evade tax is illegal and undermines public revenue.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Units 4 & 5; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: In order to execute their duties properly and fully, governments in the contemporary world need
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a budget reduction.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a continuous monitoring and influencing by citizens.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: to be given an absolute and an unchecked freedom.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: an opposition party to check than daily.

explanation.solution_text_en: Democratic government benefits from continuing citizen oversight, participation and lawful influence. Giving government absolute unchecked freedom contradicts accountability and limited government.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3
