questions.question_text_en: Creating civic societies and strengthening their contributions is very important in
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: improving society's living conditions in various ways.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: providing better salary for the employees.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: helping one's relatives with job opportunities.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: defending the sovereignty of the country.

explanation.solution_text_en: Civil-society organizations can organize voluntary action, advocate public interests, provide services and strengthen community capacity. Their civic value is broader than improving employee pay or helping relatives.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and civic participation

questions.question_text_en: Unfair treatment of women could be expressed through
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: promoting them to be good fighters in the air force.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: allowing them to ascend to queenship to rule society.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: they were denied the right to own inherit land.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: marriage and the formation of family.

explanation.solution_text_en: Denying women equal inheritance or property rights is a clear form of discriminatory treatment. Equal legal and economic rights are central to non-discrimination and gender equality.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: What were the reasons for ethno-linguistic groups to be treated unequally in Ethiopia's past?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Accepting unity in diversity.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Looking for the future to take care of their needs and aspirations.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Absence of knowledge regarding the existence of different linguistic groups in Ethiopia.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Government failures to understand multiculturalism more blessing than a curse.

explanation.solution_text_en: When governments fail to recognize and accommodate multicultural diversity, ethno-linguistic communities may experience unequal treatment. Current citizenship teaching emphasizes seeing diversity as a social resource to be managed fairly.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5 & 6

questions.question_text_en: How do we make justice prevail in society?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Through the properly functioning of the judiciary system.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Promoting industrialization.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: By way of enhancing agro-industry.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Through the promotion of development in agriculture.

explanation.solution_text_en: A properly functioning, independent and impartial justice system applies law, protects rights and provides remedies when disputes or violations occur. That is directly connected with making justice effective in society.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance / rule of law

questions.question_text_en: What roles do citizens have in the exercise of justice?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: To fail to react when an official violates the exercise of justice.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To be onlooker when injustice is being made on others.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Paying tax and do other things that could help enhance justice.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To appreciate officials when doing injustice or other people.

explanation.solution_text_en: Citizens support justice by fulfilling lawful civic duties, contributing to public institutions and responding constructively to injustice. Remaining silent or praising injustice undermines justice.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 & 3; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5

questions.question_text_en: What is right regarding the traditional justice system in Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education 2013/2014 E.C. Booklet 054

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Traditional justice systems afford to exist without the conventional courts.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Traditional justice system could play the role of complementing the conventional court.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Conventional courts and traditional ones are mutually exclusive.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Traditional justice systems and conventional courts are the same.

explanation.solution_text_en: Indigenous or traditional conflict-resolution institutions can complement formal courts by resolving appropriate community disputes through locally legitimate processes. They are neither identical to nor necessarily substitutes for the formal judicial system.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 10 - Unit 4
